correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge3\), the incidence identity \(BB^{\mathsf T}=(n-2)I+J\) determines the three invariant eigenspaces and a strictly positive definite shape. The unique positive quadratic root satisfies \(t^2mD=T\). Each edge-coordinate facet variance then equals its squared slack \(a^2\) and each vertex-degree facet variance equals \(b^2\), proving containment and tangency on all \(m+n\) facets. The explicitly positive weights \(\alpha=T/m\) and \(\beta=T/(2mt)\) cancel the first moment because the degree normals sum to twice the all-ones vector. Their exact second moment is \(\Sigma^{1/2}[\alpha I/a^2+\beta B^{\mathsf T}B/b^2]\Sigma^{1/2}=I\). John’s theorem proves global optimality and uniqueness even among nonsymmetric ellipsoids; nonproportional facet normals give distinct contacts. A standalone source verifier reconstructed all matrices in dimensions \(3\le n\le10\), checked \(216\) facet tangencies and all moment entries. Only the exact algebra proves the infinite family.

value.rationale: The complete-graph fractional matching polytope is the canonical nonbipartite half-integral matching relaxation. The theorem solves its natural Euclidean extremal inscribed ellipsoid exactly for every \(n\ge3\), including center, full constant/star/cycle spectral splitting, exact volume, and every one of \(m+n\) distinct facet contacts. The nontrivial positive-root parameter and explicit John weights distinguish a complete metric classification from a routine substitution, finite table or generic optimizer. The result has natural potential use for geometric rounding, normalization and quantitative comparisons of relaxations, without claiming unproved downstream theorems.
